experiment: Fast path pristine global zero-capture RegExp replacement
decision: retain; the isolated M4 /o/g loop retired 81.25% fewer instructions in 11 alternating pairs with byte-identical output; median workload RSS increased 160 KiB

source.candidate_also_contains: The independently measured property-add transition cache; this replacement loop does not construct ordinary user objects.

measurement.kind: 11 alternating production-binary instruction-retirement pairs, CJS-shaped; each workload subtracts its same-binary matched control
measurement.workload: var subject = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog; foo and ooo."; var iterations = 50000; var pattern = /o/g; function run(){var result=subject;for(var i=0;i<iterations;i++)result=subject.replace(pattern,"0");return result;} console.log(run());
measurement.control: var subject = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog; foo and ooo."; var iterations = 50000; function run(){var result=subject;for(var i=0;i<iterations;i++)result=subject;return result;} console.log(run());
measurement.workload_output: The quick br0wn f0x jumps 0ver the lazy d0g; f00 and 000.
measurement.scope_limit: Focused microbenchmark only; no V8-v7 fixture confirmation or Task 61 qualification is claimed.

implementation: For RegExp.prototype[Symbol.replace] calls that reach this builtin, use a direct matcher loop only for a global intrinsic RegExp with zero captures, no own exec/flags/accessor shadow, writable own data lastIndex, and unchanged intrinsic RegExp prototype exec/flags/flag accessors. Other cases use the observable generic algorithm. The fast path resets lastIndex at entry and completion, advances Unicode empty matches by code point, and uses the existing replacement-substitution semantics.

cases: global no-match and match lastIndex reset
empty global Unicode and sticky matches
callback generic fallback and callback count
own global and unicode shadow properties

verification.regression_fixed: The repeated empty-match search previously did not terminate when the next Unicode search offset exceeded the input length. find_from and find_from_utf16 now return no match for an out-of-range start; the regression is covered by empty_match_search_past_input_end_terminates.
